name: Korean Demilitarized Zone
blurb: A fenced-off strip where cranes, water deer and gorals found sanctuary.

tip.title: Remove the rice fields
tip.text: Cranes, geese and boar lean on rice gleanings in winter. Remove Rice and watch the cranes, geese and the predators and scavengers above them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: A tall wetland grass that forms dense stands along rivers and marshes. Water deer shelter in tall reeds, and red-crowned cranes nest in tall-grass wetlands.

nodes.name: Rice paddies
nodes.desc: Farmland and paddies along the zone edges. Rice gleanings are an important winter food for red-crowned cranes in East Asia.

nodes.name: Mongolian oak
nodes.desc: A dominant oak of Korean mountain forests whose acorns feed many animals, from rodents to gorals.

nodes.name: Grasses & meadow herbs
nodes.desc: Bristle-grass, dandelion, clover and other open-ground plants that geese and small herbivores graze.

nodes.name: Chinese water deer
nodes.desc: Lives among tall reeds, swamps and fields along rivers. Wikipedia says the DMZ has given it protected habitat, and that its Korean boom is linked to the loss of tigers and leopards.

nodes.name: Long-tailed goral
nodes.desc: A cliff-dwelling goat-antelope that eats grasses in summer and twigs, leaves and acorns in winter. A small endangered population lives in the DMZ.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats plants, small animals and carrion. GloBI records show it eating field mice, geese and snakes near the zone.

nodes.name: Greater white-fronted goose
nodes.desc: A winter visitor that grazes grasses, clover and dandelion in open fields.

nodes.name: Striped field mouse
nodes.desc: A small rodent of fields and grassland that eats seeds and grain, and is food for many predators.

nodes.name: Korean hare
nodes.desc: A hare of grassy and scrubby ground that feeds on plants.

nodes.name: Red-crowned crane
nodes.desc: An omnivorous wetland crane that eats fish, amphibians, insects, rodents and small reptiles, plus rice and reeds in winter. Wintering birds use the Korean peninsula.

nodes.name: Raccoon dog
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid of Korean woods and farmland that eats small animals, plants and carrion.

nodes.name: Siberian weasel
nodes.desc: A small carnivore that hunts mice and hares; GloBI records also list birds and a leopard cat among its prey.

nodes.name: Leopard cat
nodes.desc: A small wild cat that hunts rodents and other small animals. Wikipedia notes it occasionally ambushes young cranes in South Korea.

nodes.name: Steppes ratsnake
nodes.desc: A non-venomous snake of fields and scrub. GloBI has records of wild boar eating it.

nodes.name: Cinereous vulture
nodes.desc: A huge scavenger that feeds mostly on carrion and winters in South Korea. GloBI has a record of it eating water deer.

nodes.name: Asian black bear
nodes.desc: Wikipedia names this endangered bear among the DMZ animals. It is a mostly plant-eating omnivore that relies on acorns and also takes carrion.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer sun and heat drive fast plant growth in the monsoon season.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Summer rains fill the rivers, marshes and paddies on which reeds and rice depend.

nodes.name: Winter cold
nodes.desc: Cold winters push cranes and geese south to the open farmland and rivers of the zone.

nodes.name: Soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients in the soil feed forest, grass and crop growth.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, carcasses and dung and return nutrients to the soil.
